1971 opposers must apologise
2026-07-12T03:36:47+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/1971-opposers-must-apologise-4221681

Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan yesterday called on those who played a controversial role during the 1971 Liberation War to candidly accept responsibility and apologise to the nation for the sake of unity.

Speaking as the special guest at a discussion organised by the Retired Armed Forces Officers’ Welfare Association (RAWA) in the capital, he said nation-building requires a return to the spirit of the Liberation War.

“We will remain united to build Bangladesh. We will not divide the country by talking about pro- and anti-independence,” the minister said, referring to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s call for national unity to build a prosperous Bangladesh.

He said it would be difficult for the nation and freedom fighters to accept those who had opposed the Liberation War unless they acknowledged their role and apologised.

“For the greater interest of the nation, they must embrace the spirit of the Liberation War and democracy,” he added.

Speaking as the chief guest, Speaker of Parliament and valiant freedom fighter Major (Retd) Hafiz Uddin Ahmed said the East Bengal Regiment put up a courageous resistance when Pakistani forces launched their brutal military crackdown in 1971.

“At that critical moment, Major Ziaur Rahman declared independence, which inspired and motivated the nation to wage the war. This is the real truth,” he said.

RAWA Club Chairman Brig Gen Abdul Haq presided over the discussion.
